simple.meaning: כְּנַנְיָה (Kᵉnanyâh) is a Hebrew word meaning “Kenanjah , an Israelite.” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: כְּנַנְיָה (H3663) appears 3 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at 1 Chronicles 15:22, with occurrences in 1 Chronicles.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to כְּנַנְיָה (H3663) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in כְּנַנְיָה (H3663) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: כְּנַנְיָה (Kᵉnanyâh) / H3663 is traced through 1 Chronicles 15:22, 1 Chronicles 15:27, 1 Chronicles 26:29 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

evidence: Lexicon or morphology identifies this as a proper name

firstOccurrence.englishText: Chenaniah, chief of the Levites, was over the singing. He taught the singers, because he was skillful.

timeline.evidenceText: Chenaniah, chief of the Levites, was over the singing. He taught the singers, because he was skillful.
David was clothed with a robe of fine linen, as were all the Levites who bore the ark, the singers, and Chenaniah the choir master with the singers; and David had an ephod of linen on him.
Of the Izharites, Chenaniah and his sons were for the outward business over Israel, for officers and judges.
